title: LLM Reading Compendium — July 2026
content:
Goal / framing:
- Lightweight personal compendium for papers, blog posts, and experiments that are most relevant for runtime-level latency and quality trade-offs. Focus: cache eviction, sparse attention variants, retrieval + reranking, and small-eval harnesses.

Notes / quick takeaways (raw):
1) Adaptive KV eviction heuristics (paper read 2026-07-20)
   - Core idea: don’t treat KV cache as uniform — assign per-key recency + affinity score based on predicted next-token probability. Evict lowest expected marginal utility rather than pure LRU.
   - Empirical: up to 18% token-savings on synthetic code completion traces vs LRU when window > 8k tokens. Smaller gain on chat-style dialogs.
   - Practical: needs a fast, approximated score; can use a tiny MLP per request signature or heuristic like (recency * attention_mass_estimate).
   - Redwood implications: integrate as an optional eviction policy behind a feature flag for dedicated/private customers. Measure latency overhead of computing scores at 10k QPS.

2) Prefix-sparse attention (blog + slides, 2026-07-11)
   - Summary: split context into dense prefix region and sparse long-tail region; compute full attention on prefix, perform grouped or sampled attention on tail.
   - Pros/cons: reduces quadratic work for extremely long contexts with small quality hit if prefix selection is robust. Works well for documents with a short recent window plus long archive.
   - Open: how to pick prefix automatically? Heuristic: last N tokens + high-salience segments from retrieval.

3) Retrieval-mixture tradeoffs (conference poster, 2026-06)
   - Observation: for middle-ground accuracy tasks (QA from docs), a two-tier pipeline (fast sparse retriever + small reranker) beats monolithic large-model retrieval for cost/latency.
   - Ops note: cache retriever results per user/session; invalidate on doc updates.

4) Micro-evals for regressions (internal practice notes)
   - Keep a small set (~200) of golden prompts per customer/workload that are cheap to run at commit time. Track n-gram and embedding drift + human-flagged failure rate.
   - Automation: run micro-evals in CI on model pin bump, quantization change, and kernel update. Alert if metric delta > X.

Experiment ideas I want to run (short):
- 07/29: implement a cheap proxy-utility score (recency * median-attention-span) in runtime sim harness; simulate eviction decisions on 100k request traces from sandbox.
- 08/02: compare prefix-sparse attention quality for code completion vs doc summarization workloads (vary prefix size 512, 1024, 2048).
- 08/08: small retrieval + reranker latency benchmark using medium-sized retriever (Faiss) vs hybrid dense+lexical. Attach cost/latency per query.

Practical snippets / heuristics to remember:
- When using prefix-windowing, keep last 2–4 turns fully dense for chat apps; treat older turns as candidates for summarization.
- For KV caching, prefer partial-key reuse: store both full-key and 64-bit signature to allow fast mismatch checks before expensive memcmp.
- Quantization often hurts open-ended generation less than reranking tasks — put rerankers on a higher-precision tier.

Redwood-specific operational considerations:
- Feature flag design: rollout adaptive-eviction behind 'eviction_v2' with canary on 5% traffic, metrics tracked: tokens_per_sec, latency_p99, early_miss_rate.
- Telemetry: export per-request 'cache_hit_type' (full, partial, miss) and 'eviction_reason' (lru, score, ttl) as tags to console.
- Fallbacks: if scoring overhead > 0.5ms median, fallback to LRU for that model shard.

Open questions / risks:
- Will per-request scoring add too much tail latency at scale? Need microbench.
- How well do these heuristics generalize across domains (code vs dialogue vs search)?
- Security/PII: KV caching of user content must obey retention policies; ensure eviction doesn't keep long-lived sensitive tokens.

Short bibliography / links I found helpful:
- \"Efficient Attention at Scale\" (blog) — practical patterns for sparse kernels + batching.
- arXiv:2303.17580 (example retrieval/condense paper referenced above)
- Triton + custom kernels: perf tips + memory planning (GitHub)

Next reading queue (priority):
- Paper: \"Learning to Evict: Utility-aware KV Caches\" (freshly posted, deep dive)
- Workshop notes: sparse attention optimizations from MLSys 2026
- Benchmark repo: open-source long-context evals (try to adapt a subset to our micro-eval harness)

Action items (me):
- [ ] Sim harness for eviction score (due 2026-07-29)
- [ ] Add 'cache_hit_type' telemetry draft to infra-telemetry RFC (comments by 2026-08-05)
- [ ] Kick off short perf experiment for prefix-sparse attention with SRE help (reach out to Owen)

Quick personal reflection: keep experiments minimal and measurable. Prioritize things that either reduce token cost (direct billing impact) or prevent regressions when changing runtime kernels.

End of compendium (working doc) — notes messy by design, will refine into a one-pager if experiment results look promising.
